> definition of `A_{m,n}` plus his assumption (1) force `C` to be the row-2 tail
> and `D` the row-1 tail, hence `m = q - r` and **`n = p - r`**. With the
> correct coordinate Lemma 5 gives

>     p - q  <=  3r - 1     for every P-position (p,q,r), UNIFORMLY in q
> ```
>

> **2. The Zeilberger state count is this document's, not Zeilberger's.** He

> 'theoretical' upper bound for the period is enormous"*; he never counts them,

# C0024 — the corrected effective Zeilberger recursion (proof)

**Claim.** For every `r >= 1` define

```
  B_c(a) := f(c+a, c) - (c+a)          (unique loser b at [c, a, .]; undefined if none)
  u_c    := N(c) - c                    (preperiod of B_c in a-coordinates)
  p_c    := period(c);  p_c := 1 for stale rows (B_c terminates)
  q_r    := lcm{ p_c : 0 <= c < r }
  m_r    := 1 + max{ B_c(a) : 0 <= c < r, a >= 0 }        (+1; max over defined values)
  U_r    := max{ u_c : 0 <= c < r }
  t_r    := max(U_r, r)
```

Then for every `r >= 1`:

```
  (i)  B_r(a) <= r      for every defined value (so    m_r <= r + 1),
  (ii) p_r <= q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r},
  (iii) u_r <= max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r},
  (iv) q_{r+1} <= q_r^2 (r + 2)^{r + 1}.
```

In particular for live rows
`N(r) = r + u_r <= r + max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}`, while for stale rows
the last P-position `(p,q,r)` satisfies
`q - r <= max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}`, hence
`N(r) <= r + 1 + max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}`.

(i) is the value bound of C0012/C0021 (`f(q,r)-q <= r+1` in these coordinates);
(ii)-(iv) are the Ultimate-Periodicity Theorem of Zeilberger with the period
and preperiod of the instant-winner sequence made explicit. Nothing in the
argument is non-effective.

---

## 0. Coordinates and normalisations

Zeilberger's `[c, a, b]` has `c` columns of height 3, `a` of height 2, `b` of
height 1, so for the position `(p,q,r)`:

```
    c = r,   a = q - r,   b = p - q.
```

`B_c(a)` is the unique `b` such that `[c,a,b]` is a loser (uniqueness is the
first family of Zeilberger's `(Rule1)`); if none exists `B_c(a)` is undefined.
Hence `B_r(a) = f(r+a, r) - (r+a)`, and the census quantity
`d(q) = f(q,r) - q` equals `B_r(q - r)` wherever a genuine P-position exists
(`f(q,r) >= q`; for live rows this is every `q >= r`).

**Preperiod in `a`.** `N(r)` is the least `q0` such that `d(q)` is
`p_r`-periodic for all `q >= q0`. Under `q = r + a` this is: `B_r(a)` is
`p_r`-periodic for all `a >= N(r) - r =: u_r`. Minimality of `q0` translates
to: `B_r(u_r - 1) != B_r(u_r - 1 + p_r)` when `u_r >= 1` (live rows).

**Stale rows.** A stale row has finitely many P-positions; the last has
`f(q*, r) = q*`, i.e. `B_r(a*) = 0` at `a* = q* - r`, and no values for
`a > a*`. The census carries `N(r) = lastlive + 1`, so `a* = N(r) - 1 - r =
u_r - 1` and `u_r = N(r) - r` is uniform. Setting `p_r := 1`, the statement
"`B_r` is `p_r`-periodic from `a = u_r`" holds vacuously (no values are defined
for `a >= u_r`).

## 1. The instant-winner sequence and its preperiod

Fix the bottom row at `r`. The losers `[c, a', b']` with `c < r` force, through
Zeilberger's Lemmas 1-3, a set `W_r(a)` of "instant winners" — the `b` such
that `[r, a, b]` is a winner implied by some game below row `r`. His Crucial
Facts give `W_r(a)` explicitly as a union of singletons:

```
    V''_{r,c}(a) = { B_c(a + r - c) }                        (from (1.3),(2.2))
    V'_{r,c}(a)  = { B_c(0) - (r-c) - a }  ∩  Z_{>=0}        (from Lemma 3)
    W_r(a)       = ⋃_{c<r} ( V''_{r,c}(a) ∪ V'_{r,c}(a) ),
```

with empty singletons discarded.

**Lemma P (period of W).** `W_r` is `q_r`-periodic for all `a >= t_r`, where
`t_r = max(U_r, r)`.

*Proof.*

- *The V'' family.* For `a >= U_r` and `c < r`, the index of the `B_c`
  evaluation is `a'' := a + r - c >= U_r + (r-c) >= u_c + 1`, using
  `r - c >= 1`. Two cases. If `c` is live, `B_c(a'')` is defined for all
  `a'' >= 0` and is `p_c`-periodic on `a'' >= u_c`. If `c` is stale, `B_c` is
  defined for `a'' <= u_c - 1` only, so for `a'' >= u_c + 1` the value is
  undefined and the singleton is empty. In both cases, on `a >= U_r` the map
  `a ↦ V''_{r,c}(a)` is `p_c`-periodic in `a` (defined values periodic; the
  stale rows are empty, hence constant). Since `p_c | q_r`, it is
  `q_r`-periodic.

- *The V' family.* For `a >= r`, `V'_{r,c}(a)` is empty for every `c < r`:
  the value is `B_c(0) - (r-c) - a <= (c+1) - (r-c) - r = 2c + 1 - 2r < 0`,
  where `B_c(0) = f(c,c)

# A sharper closed-form bound on N(r): the lcm recursion is linear, not quadratic

**Claim.** Let `f(q,r)` be the unique `p` such that `(p,q,r)` is a P-position of
3-row Chomp (Brouwer recurrence); for each fixed `r`, let `N(r)` be the least
`q0 >= r` such that `f(q,r)-q` is periodic for all `q >= q0` (for a row with
only finitely many P-positions, `N(r)` is the least `q` with `f(q,r) < q`). Then

```
  N(r) <= r + h(r),    h(r) = 11 + r + sum_{k=2}^{r} g(k) (k+2)^{k+1},
  g(1) = 1,   g(r+1) = g(r) · (r+2)^{r+1},
```

so `g(r) = prod_{k=1}^{r-1} (k+2)^{k+1}` and

```
  log_2 g(r) = sum_{k=1}^{r-1} (k+1) log_2(k+2) = O(r^2 log r),
  N(r) <= 2^{O(r^2 log r)}.
```

This is an explicit, computable, closed-form bound; every quantity on the right
is a function of `r` alone. It is strictly sharper than the `2^{2^{O(r)}}`
bound obtained from the quadratic lcm recursion: the correct recursion is
**linear** in `q_r`, not quadratic.

---

## 0. Standing inputs (same as the companion proof; stated as black boxes)

**Input 1 (value bound, prior art).** For all `q >= r >= 0`,
`f(q,r) <= q + r + 1`. In Zeilberger coordinates `[c,a,b] = [r, q-r, p-q]` with
`B_c(a) = f(c+a,c)-(c+a)`, every defined value satisfies `B_c(a) <= c+1`.

**Input 2 (finite-state recursion).** With `u_c = N(c)-c`, `p_c` = the period of
`B_c` in `a` (`p_c := 1` if `B_c` terminates), `q_r = lcm{p_c : 0 <= c < r}`,
`m_r = 1 + max{B_c(a) : 0 <= c < r, a >= 0}`, `t_r = max(max_{c<r} u_c, r)`:

```
  (i)  m_r <= r + 1,
  (ii) p_r <= q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r},
  (iii) u_r <= 1 + max(t_r, m_r) + q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r}     (all rows),
```

and the state `S_a = (a mod q_r; L_{a-1}, ..., L_{a-m_r})` is deterministic from
`a >= max(t_r, m_r)`, with at most `q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}` states.

## 1. The sharpened lcm bound (the one improvement over the companion proof)

The companion proof derived `q_{r+1} <= q_r^2 (r+2)^{r+1}` from
`q_{r+1} = lcm(q_r, p_r) <= q_r p_r` together with (ii). That loses a factor
`q_r` unnecessarily. The pigeonhole itself gives the sharper statement directly:

**Lemma A' (linear lcm recursion).** `q_{r+1} <= q_r (m_r + 1)^{m_r} <= q_r (r+2)^{r+1}`.

*Proof.* Run the C0024 pigeonhole from `a = A0 = max(t_r, m_r)`. Among the
`S + 1` consecutive states `S_{A0}, ..., S_{A0+S}`, where
`S = q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}`, two coincide: `S_{a1} = S_{a2}` with
`A0 <= a1 < a2 <= A0 + S`. Because the state carries the phase `a mod q_r`,
`a1 ≡ a2 (mod q_r)`, so `s := a2 - a1` is a multiple of `q_r`. The transition
is deterministic from `A0` on, so the entire future repeats with period `s`:
`L_a = B_r(a)` is `s`-periodic for all `a >= a1`. Hence `s` is a period of the
(eventually periodic) row-`r` sequence, so the fundamental period divides it:
`p_r | s`. Therefore `s` is a common multiple of `q_r` and `p_r`, and

```
  q_{r+1} = lcm(q_r, p_r)  |  s  <=  S = q_r (m_r+1)^{m_r}.
```

The second inequality is (i): `m_r <= r+1`, and `m -> (m+1)^m` is increasing. ∎

The point: one does **not** need to multiply (ii)'s bound on `p_r` by `q_r`;
the pigeonhole produces a common multiple of `q_r` and `p_r` directly.

## 2. The unrolling

Define the a priori sequence `g` by the linear recursion:

```
  g(1) = 1,      g(r+1) = g(r) · (r+2)^{r+1}.
```

**Lemma B' (a priori lcm bound).** `q_r <= g(r)` for every `r >= 1`.

*Proof.* Row `0` has period 1, so `q_1 = 1 = g(1)`. Inductively, Lemma A' gives

```
  q_{r+1} <= q_r (r+2)^{r+1} <= g(r) (r+2)^{r+1} = g(r+1).   ∎
```

Define the a priori sequence `h` by

```
  h(1) = 12,      h(r) = 1 + h(r-1) + g(r) (r+2)^{r+1}   (r >= 2).
```

**Lemma C' (a priori preperiod bound).** `u_r = N(r) - r <= h(r)` for every
`r >= 1`, hence `N(r) <= r + h(r)` for all rows.

*Proof.* Identical to the companion proof: (iii) gives
`u_r <= 1 + max(t_r, m_r) + q_r(m_r+1)^{m_r}`; by induction `u_c <= h(c)` for
`c < r` and `h` is increasing, so `t_r <= max(h(r-1), r)`; `m_r <= r+1`; and
`q_r <= g(r)`. Since `h(r-1) >= 12 > r+1`, the max is `h(r-1)`, giving
`u_r <= 1 + h(r-1) + g(r)

"""Thin Python wrapper around GROUND_TRUTH/solver.cpp.

Builds the binary on demand (g++, clang++ or MSVC) and parses its four output
modes.  Nothing here reimplements the recurrence: the C++ file is the single
source of truth, and this module only moves bytes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SRC = HERE / "solver.cpp"
EXE = HERE / ("solver.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "solver")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- build
def _msvc_env() -> dict | None:
    """Locate a 64-bit MSVC toolchain via vswhere and return its environment."""
    vswhere = Path(os.environ.get("ProgramFiles(x86)", "C:/Program Files (x86)")) \
        / "Microsoft Visual Studio/Installer/vswhere.exe"
    if not vswhere.exists():
        return None
    try:
        root = subprocess.run(
            [str(vswhere), "-products", "*", "-latest", "-property", "installationPath"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
            check=True).stdout.strip()
    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, OSError):
        return None
    vcvars = Path(root) / "VC/Auxiliary/Build/vcvars64.bat"
    if not root or not vcvars.exists():
        return None
    out = subprocess.run(["cmd", "/c", f'"{vcvars}" >nul 2>&1 && set'],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)

We have:

$$
L_4=mex(I_4 \cup \{L_3-1, L_2-2, L_1-3, L_0-4 \} )=mex(\{ 0,1,2\})=3 \quad.
$$

Now we can already {\it guess} a pattern, $L_a=3$ for $a \geq 2$.
Let's try and prove it by induction using $(FundamentalRecurrence)$.
We have just established it for $a=2,3,4$. 
For $a \geq 5$ we have, by the inductive hypothesis, that 
the set of non-negative integers in
$$
I_a \cup \{ L_{a-1}-1, L_{a-2}-2, \dots, L_0 -a \}
$$
is really finite, namely 
$$
I_a \cup \{ 3-1, 3-2, 3-3 \}= \{0,1,2\}
$$
and its $mex$ equals $3$. \halmos


{\bf The Ultimate-Periodicity Phenomenon}

Now assume that the sequence of sets $I_a$ describing the
instant winners is not arbitrary, but is
{\it ultimately-periodic}. In other words,
starting at a certain place $a_0$, there is a (minimal) period
$p$ such that $I_a=I_{a+p}$ for $a>a_0$.

Now we are on more secure grounds. Ultimately-Periodic Sequences
are {\it finite} objects, and hence meaningful. To describe such
a sequence all we have to do is specify the non-periodic head
$I_0, \dots, I_{a_0}$ followed by the period 
$I_{a_0+1},I_{a_0+2}, \dots , I_{a_0+p}$ that keeps repeating.

{\bf Two Immediate Consequences of} $(FundamentalRecurrence)$

{\bf Lemma Bounded}: If the sets $I_a$ are (uniformly) bounded,
and $M-1$ is an upper bound, (i.e. $max(I_a) \leq M-1$ for all $a >0$)
then $L_a \leq M$, for all $a>0$.

{\bf Proof}: This follows immediately from the fact that
$mex(S) \leq max(S)+1$, and induction on $a$.

{\bf Ultimate-Periodicity Theorem}: If $I_a$ is ultimately-periodic
then the sequence $L_a$ either terminates (with the last value
being $0$), or else is ultimately-periodic.

{\bf Proof:} Since $I_a$ is ultimately-periodic the set of
finite sets $\{ I_a  \,\, ; \,\, a >0  \}$ is finite, and hence bounded.
Let $M-1$ be the (least) upper bound. By Lemma {\bf Bounded},
$L_a \leq M$. Since negative integers in a set do not 
affect its $mex$ (recall that $mex(S)$ is the smallest
{\it non-negative} integer in the complement of $S$),
the hitherto ``infinite memory'' recurrence
$(FundamentalRecurrence)$, where to know the value of
$L_a$ you have to remember {\it all} your past, now
becomes a ``finite memory'' recurrence, where you only
have to remember what happened in the last $M$ days.
$$
L_a= mex(I_a \cup \{ L_{a-1}-1, L_{a-2}-2, \dots, L_{a-M}-M \}) \quad.
\eqno(BoundedFundamentalRecurrence)
$$

S_a:=(I_a \,\,;\,\,
L_{a-1},L_{a-2}, \dots, L_{a-M} )

def f_at(cen: dict[int, dict], q: int, r: int) -> int | None:
    """f(q,r) from a census descriptor, for q past the column's preperiod."""
    c = cen[r]
    if c["cls"] == "stale":
        return c["dconst"] if q >= c["deathq"] else None
    if q < c["N"]:
        return None
    return q + c["dvals"][(q - c["N"]) % c["period"]]

"""Structure of the preperiod u_r = N(r) - r from the 50000-row census.

Questions:
  Q1  u_r <= r ?  (equiv N(r) <= 2r; C0030 numerics say yes for r>=2)
  Q2  u_r <= u_{r-1} + 1 ?  (inductive increment bound)
  Q3  u_r - u_{r-1} distribution; u_r vs U_r = max_{c<r} u_c
  Q4  u_r vs t_r = max(U_r, r):  is u_r <= t_r always?  (i.e. the row goes
      periodic BEFORE its driver W_r does)
  Q5  incremental gaps: u_r - max(u_c : c<r and same period class)?
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

CEN = Path("GROUND_TRUTH/cache/census_50000.tsv")

rows = []  # (r, cls, period, N)
with open(CEN) as fh:
    header = fh.readline()
    for line in fh:
        parts = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        r = int(parts[0]); cls = parts[1]
        period = int(parts[2]); N = int(parts[3])
        rows.append((r, cls, period, N))

u = {r: N - r for (r, cls, p, N) in rows}
cls = {r: c for (r, c, p, N) in rows}
per = {r: (p if c == "live" else 1) for (r, c, p, N) in rows}  # p:=1 stale

R = max(u)
print(f"rows 0..{R}")

# Q1: u_r <= r ?
viol = [(r, u[r]) for r in u if u[r] > r]
print("Q1 u_r <= r : violations =", len(viol), viol[:10])
viol2 = [(r, u[r]) for r in u if r >= 2 and u[r] > r]
print("   (r>=2)    : violations =", len(viol2), viol2[:10])
print("   max u_r/r for r>=2:", max((u[r]/r, r) for r in u if r >= 2))
print("   max u_r/r overall:", max((u[r]/r, r) for r in u))

# Q2: u_r <= u_{r-1} + 1 ?
viol = [(r, u[r], u[r-1]) for r in sorted(u) if r >= 1 and u[r] > u[r-1] + 1]
print("Q2 u_r <= u_{r-1}+1 : violations =", len(viol), viol[:10])

# Q3: increments
from collections import Counter
inc = Counter(u[r] - u[r-1] for r in sorted(u) if r >= 1)
print("Q3 increment distribution:", dict(sorted(inc.items())))

# Q4: u_r <= t_r = max(U_r, r)
U = 0
viol = []
for r in sorted(u):
    if r >= 1 and u[r] > max(U, r):
        viol.append((r, u[r], U))
    U = max(U, u[r])
print("Q4 u_r <= max(U_r,r) : violations =", len(viol), viol[:10])

# Q4b: u_r <= U_r + 1 ?  (no growth beyond running max by more than 1)
U = 0
viol = []
for r in sorted(u):
    if r >= 1 and u[r] > U + 1:
        viol.append((r, u[r], U))
    U = max(U, u[r])
print("Q4b u_r <= U_r+1 : violations =", len(viol), viol[:10])

# Q5: same-period-class runs: u_r minus running max within class
runmax = {}
gaps = Counter()
big = []
for r in sorted(u):
    k = (cls[r], per[r])
    m = runmax.get(k, -10**9)
    if m > -10**9:
        gaps[u[r] - m] += 1
        if u[r] - m > 2:
            big.append((r, cls[r], per[r], u[r], m))
    runmax[k] = max(m, u[r])
print("Q5 gap-to-class-runningmax distribution:", dict(sorted(gaps.items())))
print("   gaps > 2:", big[:10])

# stale vs live stats
for cl in ("stale", "live"):
    us = [u[r] for r in u if cls[r] == cl]
    print(f"{cl}: n={len(us)} max u_r={max(us)} min={min(us)}")

# period-1 live rows: u_r <= u_{r-1}+1 restricted?
viol = [(r, u[r], u[r-1]) for r in sorted(u) if r >= 1 and cls[r] == "live"
        and per[r] == 1 and u[r] > u[r-1] + 1]
print("Q2 restricted to period-1 live rows: violations =", len(viol), viol[:10])

# What is u_r - u_{r-1} for consecutive LIVE rows?
inc_live = Counter(u[r] - u[r-1] for r in sorted(u) if r >= 2 and cls[r] == "live" and cls[r-1] == "live")
print("live-live increment distribution:", dict(sorted(inc_live.items())))

# largest u_r values, and rows where u_r > r - small
top = sorted(u.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
print("top u_r:", top)
"}

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Abstract mex-shift machine: worst-case L-transient.

Machine (Zeilberger's Fundamental Recurrence with V' merged into the trail):
    H_{a+1} = dec(H_a) union {k_a - 1},   k_a = mex(V[a mod q] union H_a),
    L_a = k_a,   dec(X) = {x-1 : x in X, x >= 1}.
Input V[0..q-1], each V[i] a subset of [0, M].  Start H_0 subset of [0, M+1].
k_a = 0 means termination (stale).  We measure, over all nonterminating runs,
the L-transient: least a0 such that L_a is periodic for all a >= a0.

Bitmask encoding: H as int, mex(V|H) by scanning bits.
"""
import sys
from itertools import product
from collections import defaultdict


def mex_bits(s: int) -> int:
    m = 0
    while s & (1 << m):
        m += 1
    return m


def run_machine(V, q, H0, M, horizon=200000):
    """Return (transient, period, terminated) for L, exact via state repetition.
    state = (a mod q, H).  L-transient computed exactly: after entry to the
    state cycle at index i with cycle length p, scan back for least a0 with
    L[a] == L[a+p] on [a0, end]."""
    seen = {}
    L = []
    H = H0
    a = 0
    while a < horizon:
        st = (a % q, H)
        if st in seen:
            i = seen[st]
            p = a - i
            # L is p-periodic on [i, a).  Find least a0 <= i with
            # L[x] == L[x+p] for all x in [a0, a-p).
            a0 = i
            while a0 > 0 and L[a0 - 1] == L[a0 - 1 + p]:
                a0 -= 1
            return (a0, p, False)
        seen[st] = a
        S = V[a % q] | H
        k = mex_bits(S)
        L.append(k)
        if k == 0:
            # terminates at a; L is finite.  transient = None (stale)
            return (None, None, True)
        H = ((H >> 1) | (1 << (k - 1)))
        a += 1
    raise RuntimeError("horizon")


def sweep(M, q, max_v_sets=None):
    """Exhaustive over all V-patterns of period q with values in [0,M],
    all H0 subsets of [0,M+1].  Return worst L-transient among nonterminating
    runs, plus argmax, and stats."""
    universe = 1 << (M + 1)           # subsets of [0, M]
    all_v = list(range(universe))
    if max_v_sets is not None and len(all_v) > max_v_sets:
        raise RuntimeError("too many")
    H_universe = 1 << (M + 2)         # subsets of [0, M+1]
    worst = -1
    arg = None
    nruns = nterm = 0
    for Vt in product(all_v, repeat=q):
        V = Vt
        for H0 in range(H_universe):
            nruns += 1
            t, p, term = run_machine(V, q, H0, M)
            if term:
                nterm += 1
                continue
            if t > worst:
                worst = t
                arg = (Vt, H0, p)
    return worst, arg, nruns, nterm


def decode(mask, hi):
    return [x for x in range(hi + 1) if mask >> x & 1]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("M q  worst_L_transient  arg(V, H0, period)")
    for M in range(1, 5):
        for q in range(1, 5):
            worst, arg, nruns, nterm = sweep(M, q)
            Vt, H0, p = arg
            Vd = [decode(v, M) for v in Vt]
            print(f"M={M} q={q} worst={worst} period={p} "
                  f"runs={nruns} term={nterm} V={Vd} H0={decode(H0, M+1)}")
            sys.stdout.flush()

{"content": "# C0032 / C0033 — the merged-trail machine and its determinism onset

This file proves two lemmas about Zeilberger's Fundamental Recurrence that
together re-found the preperiod analysis on a *deterministic machine with an
explicit start time*. Both lemmas are exact algebraic reformulations; nothing
here is conjectural.

Notation (same as proofs/C0024.md). Fix the third row `r`. For `c < r`:

```
  B_c(x)   = f(c+x, c) - (c+x)                  (loser coordinate of row c)
  u_c      = N(c) - c                           (row c preperiod, a-coords)
  p_c      = period of row c (p_c := 1 for stale rows)
  q_r      = lcm{ p_c : c < r }
```

Zeilberger's instant winners at `[r, a, .]` decompose (C0024, Section 1) as

```
  V''_{r,c}(a) = { B_c(a + r - c) }                        (defined values)
  V'_{r,c}(a)  = { B_c(0) - (r-c) - a }  ∩ Z_{>=0}
  W_r(a)       = V''(a) ∪ V'(a),     V''(a) = ⋃_{c<r} V''_{r,c}(a),
                                    V'(a) = ⋃_{c<r} V'_{r,c}(a),
```

and the Fundamental Recurrence is

```
  L_a = mex( W_r(a) ∪ { L_{a-1} - 1, L_{a-2} - 2, ... } ),      (FR)
```

mex over the **non-negative** integers, `L_a = B_r(a)`, `L_a = 0`
terminating the row (stale), all `L_a` defined and `>= 1` for live rows.
Write `dec(X) = { x-1 : x ∈ X, x >= 1 }`.

## C0032 (Lemma M — merged-trail machine)

**Claim.** Define `H_0 := V'(0)` and iterate

```
  k_a = mex( V''(a) ∪ H_a ),      H_{a+1} = dec(H_a) ∪ { k_a - 1 }.    (M)
```

(with the convention that `k_a = 0` terminates). Then `k_a = L_a` and
`H_a = V'(a) ∪ T_a` for all `a`, where `T_a = { L_{a-i} - i : i >= 1 }
∩ Z_{>=0}` is the trail of (FR).

**Proof.** Two independent identities, both one line.

1. `V'(a+1) = dec(V'(a))`. Indeed `V'(a) = { B_c(0)-(r-c)-a : c < r } ∩ Z_{>=0}`
   and `dec` maps the singleton at value `v` to the singleton at `v-1`,
   discarding `v = 0`; that is exactly the `a ↦ a+1` shift of the family.

2. `T_{a+1} = dec(T_a) ∪ { L_a - 1 }` (for `L_a >= 1`; if `L_a = 0` the row
   terminates). Indeed
   `T_{a+1} = { L_{a+1-i} - i : i >= 1 } ∩ Z_{>=0}
            = ( { L_a - 1 } ∪ { L_{a-j} - (j+1) : j >= 1 } ) ∩ Z_{>=0}
            = { L_a - 1 } ∪ dec(T_a)`.

Both families therefore obey the *same* decay rule, so their union
`H_a := V'(a) ∪ T_a` obeys `H_{a+1} = dec(H_a) ∪ { L_a - 1 }`, and (FR)
reads `L_a = mex( V''(a) ∪ V'(a) ∪ T_a ) = mex( V''(a) ∪ H_a )`. With
`H_0 = V'(0) ∪ T_0 = V'(0)` (empty trail at `a = 0`), induction on `a` in (M)
gives `k_a = L_a` at every step. ∎

**Consequences.** (a) The whole row-`r` dynamics is a deterministic machine
driven by the single input sequence `V''(a)`; the `V'` family needs no separate
handling. (b) The state `(τ; H)` with `τ = a mod q_r` is deterministic as soon
as `V''` is `q_r`-periodic; the state space is `q_r · 2^{m_r}` sets `H ⊆
[0, m_r]`, but the *shape* of `H` is heavily constrained (see the attractor
discussion in NOTES.md).

## C0033 (Lemma S — determinism onset)

**Claim.** `V''(a)` is `q_r`-periodic for all `a >= σ_r`, where

```
  σ_r = max_{c<r} N(c) - r =: M_{r-1} - r,      M_{r-1} = max_{c<r} N(c).
```

In particular the machine (M) is autonomous (deterministic given its state and
phase) from `a = max(σ_r, 0)` on, and the L-sequence is generated by a
deterministic finite machine from `a = σ_r` on.

**Proof.** Componentwise. Fix `c < r`. The component `V''_{r,c}(a) =
{ B_c(a + r - c) }` evaluates `B_c` at argument `x = a + r - c`, and `x >=
u_c = N(c) - c` iff `a >= N(c) - r`. On arguments `x >= u_c`, `B_c` is either
`p_c`-periodic (live `c`) or undefined forever (stale `c`); in both cases the
map `a ↦ V''_{r,c}(a)` is `p_c`-periodic on `a >= N(c) - r`. Since `p_c | q_r`,
it is `q_r`-periodic there. Taking the maximum over `c < r` of the thresholds
gives `σ_r = max_{c<r} (N(c) - r) = M_{r-1} - r`. ∎

**Remark (why σ_r, not t_r).** C0024's Lemma P made `W_r` periodic only at
`t_r = max(U_r, r)`, because it waited for the `V'` family to extinguish
(`a >= r`). Lemma M absorbs `V'` into the state, so only `V''` matters for
autonomy, and `V''` goes periodic at `σ_r = M_{r-1} - r`, which is *strictly
earlier*: numerically `σ_r ≈ (√2-1) r ≈ 0.414 r` while `t_r = r`. The observed
preperiod `u_r = N(r) - r ≈ 0.414 r` tracks `σ_r`, not `t_r`; the census gives
`u_r - σ_r = N(r) - max_{c<r} N(c) ∈ [-4, 6]` for all `r <= 50000`
(claim C0034). So the right conjecture is an O(1) convergence bound of the
machine (M) after determinism onset, which would give
`N(r) <= max_{c<r} N(c) + K` and hence `N(r) <= K·r` by a one-line induction.

## Numerical validation

`scratch/machine_validate.py`, against the GROUND_TRUTH solver:

- **V1** machine (M) reproduces `f(r+a,r) - (r+a)` exactly, all rows `r <= 300`,
  all `a` in range, stale rows including their terminating `0`;
- **V2** `V''` is `q_r`-periodic from `a = σ_r` on sample rows (0 failures);
- **V3** `u_r - σ_r <= 4` for `r <= 300`; the 50000-row census gives the range
  `[-4, 6]` (C0034).

Abstract-machine sweeps (`scratch/machine_abstract.py`) show the worst-case
L-transient of (M) over all q-periodic inputs `V ⊆ [0,M]` grows at least like
`~M·q` (12 at `M=4, q=3`), so an O(1) bound is **false for general inputs** and
must use the chomp-specific structure of `V''` and of the state reached at
`σ_r` (the interval attractor; see NOTES.md).

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Chomp machine 'junk' at determinism onset a = sigma_r.

Define, at step a: k = mex(V''(a) u H), holes = [0,k-1] \ H (must be plugged
by V'' by def of mex), excess = H \ [0,k-1] (chips strictly above the mex).
'Clean' state := few holes, few excess chips, excess height small.

For every row r <= R: run the machine, record at a = sigma_r (and at a=0):
|holes|, |excess|, max excess height, and the lock delay u_r - sigma_r.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
from GROUND_TRUTH import chomp

CEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "GROUND_TRUTH/cache/census_50000.tsv"


def load_census():
    N, cls, per = {}, {}, {}
    with open(CEN) as fh:
        fh.readline()
        for line in fh:
            if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip():
                continue
            p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            r = int(p[0]); cls[r] = p[1]; per[r] = int(p[2]); N[r] = int(p[3])
    return N, cls, per


def main(R, AMAX):
    N, cls, per = load_census()
    qmax = R + AMAX + R + 10
    F = chomp.table(R, qmax)

    def B(c, x):
        q = c + x
        if q > qmax or c > R or x < 0:
            return None
        if cls[c] == "stale" and q >= N[c]:
            return None
        return F[q][c] - q

    def dec(S):
        return {x - 1 for x in S if x >= 1}

    def mex(S):
        m = 0
        while m in S:
            m += 1
        return m

    worst_sigma = (0, 0, 0, 0)   # (holes+excess, row, holes, excess)
    worst_excess_h = (0, 0)
    rows = []
    for r in range(1, R + 1):
        sigma = max(N[c] for c in range(0, r)) - r
        u = N[r] - r
        if sigma < 0:
            sigma = 0
        H = set()
        for a in range(0, max(sigma, u) + 1):
            Vpp = {B(c, a + r - c) for c in range(0, r)}
            Vpp = {v for v in Vpp if v is not None}
            if a == 0:
                H = set()
                for c in range(0, r):
                    v = B(c, 0) - (r - c)
                    if v >= 0:
                        H.add(v)
            k = mex(Vpp | H)
            if a == sigma:
                holes = [h for h in range(0, k) if h not in H]
                excess = [h for h in H if h > k]
                tot = len(holes) + len(excess)
                rows.append((r, k, len(holes), len(excess),
                             max(excess) - k if excess else 0, u - sigma))
                if tot > worst_sigma[0]:
                    worst_sigma = (tot, r, len(holes), len(excess))
                if excess and max(excess) - k > worst_excess_h[0]:
                    worst_excess_h = (max(excess) - k, r)
            if k == 0:
                break
            H = dec(H) | {k - 1}
    print(f"rows measured: {len(rows)}")
    print("worst (holes+excess) at sigma:", worst_sigma)
    print("worst excess height above k at sigma:", worst_excess_h)
    from collections import Counter
    print("holes distribution:", Counter(x[2] for x in rows))
    print("excess distribution:", Counter(x[3] for x in rows))
    print("excess-height distribution:", Counter(x[4] for x in rows))
    print("lock delay u-sigma distribution:", Counter(x[5] for x in rows))
    # correlation: does (holes+excess) predict lock delay?
    big = [x for x in rows if x[2] + x[3] >= 4]
    print("rows with >=4 junk at sigma:", big[:20])
    # print worst few rows
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: -(x[2] + x[3]))
    print("top junk rows (r, k, holes, excess, excess_h, delay):")
    for x in rows[:15]:
        print("  ", x)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    R = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 300
    AMAX = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 400
    main(R, AMAX)

text: MAJOR structural identification. In `r=626` the delay-5 comes from a single hole descending at speed 1, plugged by `V''` for 4 steps (a "staircase"), then unplugged and instantly filled. Algebraically: `V''(a) = {f(a+r, c) − (a+r) : c < r}` is just the **column `q = a+r` of the f-table**, so a descending staircase of length t is exactly **a fixed `p*` occurring as `f(q, c)` in t consecutive columns `q`**. The lock delay is controlled by "max run of consecutive `q` sharing a `p*`" — a clean combinatorial quantity of `f` itself. Test it:

### 2026-10-02 -- Inductive increment bound u_r <= u_{r-1} + 1 is false
**Tried:** prove N(r) <= 2r by showing the preperiod grows by at most 1 per row.
**Failed because:** 18340 violations to r=50000; increments u_r - u_{r-1} range
{-5,...,+5} with mode +2. N is not Lipschitz in r.
**Revisit if:** never; the running-max form (C0037) is the viable inductive
statement (N(r) <= max_{c<r} N(c) + K does not need consecutive-row control).

### 2026-10-02 -- Machine transient bounded by f(p,q) alone (independent of M)
**Tried:** prove the mex-shift machine's L-transient depends only on the input
period q and realized period p; that plus bounded periods would give N(r)<=C*r.
**Failed because:** transient grows ~2.4*M even at q=1, p=1 (random search:
t=96 at M=40; exhaustive t=12 at M=4,q=3). Pathological starts are sparse V
plus sparse H0; the decaying junk crosses the mex band for Theta(M) steps.
**Revisit if:** a bound in terms of (p, q, junk measure) where the chomp state at
sigma_r has provably small junk -- but the junk at sigma_r is NOT small in the
naive sense (holes at depths up to 175 below the mex; see below).

### 2026-10-02 -- Lock delay <= staircase length of V'' plug runs (as stated)
**Tried:** bound the machine lock delay by the length of descending plug
staircases in V'', identified with runs of a fixed p* as valid f-values in
consecutive columns (C0035).
**Failed because:** the table has runs of length 177 (p*=425, columns 249..425)
while the observed delay is <= 6. Either the long runs sit at hole heights far
from the mex band, or involve c >= r for the row in question, or the descending
hole synchronises into a p-cycle (periodic holes are fine -- L can be periodic
while holes descend cyclically, e.g. the r=120 p=2 attractor). A refined
statement must track the hole height relative to k and the c<r restriction.
**Revisit if:** one can prove that plug runs at heights within O(1) of the mex
are short for c<r (a 'near-mex staircase bound'), or that a descending hole
syncs into the attractor within O(1) of determinism regardless of run length.

### 2026-10-02 -- 'Clean state at determinism onset' in the naive sense
**Tried:** show the machine state at a=sigma_r is an interval minus O(1) junk
near the mex, which would lock in O(1) steps.
**Failed because:** holes below the mex at sigma_r sit at scattered depths (187
holes over 287 rows to r=300, depths 1..175 below k), and some rows show big
excess (up to 45 chips above a small mex k=3, which nonetheless lock in <=3
steps). The state is NOT naively clean; the locking mechanism is subtler (a
hole at the mex position is filled by the injection within 1 step, and holes
plugged by V'' either descend into the mex and get filled, or sync into a
p-cycle).
**Revisit if:** a potential function on (k, hole multiset, excess) can be found
that decreases within O(1) steps on chomp inputs.
EOF

## Addendum 2 (referee gap, t=0.8 run of 2026-10-02): why p_r | s

The referee flagged "p_r | s" as true but unproved. The missing standard step:

**Lemma (periods form a group).** If a sequence is purely periodic on a tail
with least period p and is also s-periodic there, then p | s.

*Proof.* Let x be periodic on [a, ∞) with least period p and with period s.
For i >= a, x_i = x_{i+g} with g = gcd(p,s): by Bezout g = ap + bs for
integers a,b; iterating the p-periodicity |b| times and the s-periodicity |a|
times (all indices stay >= a since we only move forward by positive multiples
of p or s... careful: Bezout coefficients may be negative). Clean version:
the set T = {t >= 0 : x_i = x_{i+t} for all i >= a} is closed under subtraction
of a smaller element (if t,t' in T with t > t', then x_i = x_{i+t-t'} for all
i >= a: indeed x_{i+t-t'} = x_{i+t} (shift by t' in T) = x_i (shift by t in T)).
A nonempty set of non-negative integers closed under subtraction is generated
by its least element g. Since p, s in T, g | p and g | s. As p is the LEAST
period, g = p, hence p | s. ∎

Applied here: the machine's L-sequence is purely periodic on [a1, ∞) with
least period p_r (p_r is BY DEFINITION the least period of the tail from u_r;
and a suffix of a purely periodic sequence has the same least period — the
tail is the repetition of a cyclic word of length p_r and a suffix is the
repetition of a cyclic shift of it, which has the same least period). Since it
is also s-periodic there (the state cycle), the lemma gives p_r | s. This is
exactly what Lemma A' needs for q_{r+1} = lcm(q_r, p_r) | s.
EOF
echo done"}

- **C0032 (proved + validated):** Zeilberger's recurrence collapses to the merged-trail machine `H_{a+1} = dec(H_a) ∪ {mex(V''(a) ∪ H_a) − 1}` — the V′ family decays exactly like the mex-trail, so one state variable drives everything. Validated exactly against the solver on rows ≤ 300.

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""POST-ONSET PLUG RUNS per row -- the quantity that controls lock delay.

Mechanism (C0035): a descending hole at height h in the machine state is
'plugged' at step a iff h in V''(a), i.e. iff p* = h + a + r occurs as a valid
value f(q, c) = p* >= q in column q = a + r with witness c < r. A plug run of
length t = t consecutive plugged steps for one descending hole = t consecutive
columns q sharing a fixed p* with witnesses c < r.

Post-onset restriction (the new content here): row r's machine is autonomous
only for a >= sigma_r, i.e. columns q >= M_{r-1} := max_{c<r} N(c). Runs visible
post-onset with witnesses c < r are the ones that can delay the lock. Stale
witness rows contribute nothing post-onset (B undefined); live witnesses give
p* = q + B_c(q-c) with B_c periodic.

Measure: for each row r <= R, max run length of consecutive q in
[M_{r-1}, M_{r-1} + W] sharing a p* with witnesses c < r (valid f(q,c) >= q).
Report distribution, clipped runs, and correlation with delay u_r - sigma_r.
Also: same without the c < r restriction (all c <= R), and restricted to
witnesses c < r AND hole heights h = p* - q below the row's attractor mex.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
from GROUND_TRUTH import chomp

CEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "GROUND_TRUTH/cache/census_50000.tsv"


def load_census():
    N, cls, per = {}, {}, {}
    with open(CEN) as fh:
        fh.readline()
        for line in fh:
            if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip():
                continue
            p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            r = int(p[0]); cls[r] = p[1]; per[r] = int(p[2]); N[r] = int(p[3])
    return N, cls, per


def main(R, W):
    N, cls, per = load_census()
    qmax = max(N[c] for c in range(0, R)) + W + 5
    print(f"building table rmax={R} qmax={qmax} ...")
    F = chomp.table(R, qmax)
    print("table built")

    def valid_vals(q, clo, chi):
        """set of p* = f(q,c) >= q for c in [clo, chi], with stale cutoff."""
        out = set()
        for c in range(clo, chi + 1):
            if c > R or q > qmax:
                continue
            if cls[c] == "stale" and q >= N[c]:
                continue
            v = F[q][c]
            if v >= q:
                out.add(v)
        return out

    dist_r = Counter()      # max run, witnesses c<r, post-onset window
    dist_all = Counter()    # max run, all witnesses c<=R
    clipped = 0
    worst = (0, 0)
    rows = []
    for r in range(1, R + 1):
        Mprev = max(N[c] for c in range(0, r)) if r > 0 else 0
        q0 = max(Mprev, 0)
        best_r = 0
        best_all = 0
        best_arg = None
        # runs: p* -> current run length over consecutive q
        run_r = {}
        run_all = {}
        for q in range(q0, q0 + W + 1):
            vals_r = valid_vals(q, 0, r - 1)
            vals_all = valid_vals(q, 0, R)
            for p in vals_r:
                run_r[p] = run_r.get(p, 0) + 1
                if run_r[p] > best_r:
                    best_r = run_r[p]
                    best_arg = (p, q)
            for p in list(run_r):
                if p not in vals_r:
                    del run_r[p]
            for p in vals_all:
                run_all[p] = run_all.get(p, 0) + 1
                if run_all[p] > best_all:
                    best_all = run_all[p]
            for p in list(run_all):
                if p not in vals_all:
                    del run_all[p]
        # runs still open at window end are clipped
        if any(v >= W for v in run_r.values()):
            clipped += 1
        dist_r[best_r] += 1
        dist_all[best_all] += 1
        delay = N[r] - Mprev
        rows.append((r, best_r, best_all, delay, best_arg))
        if best_r > worst[0]:
            worst = (best_r, r)
    print(f"rows: {len(rows)}, clipped (open run at window end): {clipped}")
    print("POST-ONSET max plug run (witnesses c<r) distribution:",
          dict(sorted(dist_r.items())))
    print("POST-ONSET max plug run (all witnesses c<=R) distribution:",
          dict(sorted(dist_all.items())))
    print("worst (run, r):", worst)
    # correlation with delay
    print("\nrun vs delay (r, run_c<r, run_all, delay, arg(p*,q_end)):")
    rows.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
    for x in rows[:20]:
        print("  ", x)
    # does run_c<r >= 3 predict delay?
    big = [x for x in rows if x[1] >= 3]
    print(f"\nrows with post-onset run >=3 (c<r): {len(big)}; "
          f"their delays: {Counter(x[3] for x in big)}")
    zero = [x for x in rows if x[1] <= 1]
    print(f"rows with run <=1: {len(zero)}; their delays: {Counter(x[3] for x in zero)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    R = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 500
    W = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 60
    main(R, W)

"""COUNTEREXAMPLE HUNT for C0039 (post-onset plug-run bound).

A plug run for row r: consecutive columns q = q0..q0+t-1 sharing a fixed valid
p* (f(q,c)=p*>=q), each column with SOME witness c < r, and post-onset
q0 >= max_{c<r} N(c) =: M_{r-1}.

Admissibility of a raw run (p*, columns, per-column witness sets):
  cstar = max over columns of (min witness c in that column)
  -> any r > cstar plugs every column; take r = cstar+1 (smallest M_{r-1}).
  run is admissible iff q0 >= M_{cstar} = max_{c<=cstar} N(c).
Report the max admissible run length and the top raw runs with verdicts.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]))
from GROUND_TRUTH import chomp

CEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "GROUND_TRUTH/cache/census_50000.tsv"


def load_N():
    N = {}
    with open(CEN) as fh:
        fh.readline()
        for line in fh:
            if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip():
                continue
            p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            N[int(p[0])] = int(p[3])
    return N


def main(R, Q):
    N = load_N()
    # running max of N(c) for the admissibility test
    Mmax = {}
    run = -1
    for c in sorted(N):
        run = max(run, N[c])
        Mmax[c] = run

    F = chomp.table(R, Q)
    # per column q: dict p* -> sorted witness list (valid only)
    col = {}
    for q in range(0, Q + 1):
        d = {}
        for c in range(0, min(q, R) + 1):
            v = F[q][c]
            if v >= q:
                d.setdefault(v, []).append(c)
        col[q] = d

    runs = []          # (length, p*, q0, cstar, admissible, M_needed)
    open_runs = {}     # p* -> [q0, cstar, len]
    for q in range(0, Q + 1):
        d = col[q]
        for p in list(open_runs):
            if p not in d:
                q0, cstar, ln = open_runs.pop(p)
                runs.append((ln, p, q0, cstar))
        for p, ws in d.items():
            mn = ws[0]
            if p in open_runs:
                open_runs[p][2] += 1
                open_runs[p][1] = max(open_runs[p][1], mn)
            else:
                open_runs[p] = [q, mn, 1]
    for p, (q0, cstar, ln) in open_runs.items():
        runs.append((ln, p, q0, cstar))

    # admissibility: q0 >= Mmax[cstar] (r = cstar+1 minimal); also r <= R-ish
    best_adm = (0,)
    n_adm_long = 0
    runs.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
    print(f"total runs: {len(runs)}; top 25 raw runs (len, p*, q0, cstar, verdict):")
    for ln, p, q0, cstar in runs[:25]:
        need = Mmax.get(cstar, 10**9)
        adm = q0 >= need
        if adm and ln > best_adm[0]:
            best_adm = (ln, p, q0, cstar, need)
        print(f"  len={ln:4d} p*={p:6d} q0={q0:6d} cstar={cstar:5d} "
              f"need q0>={need}  -> {'ADMISSIBLE' if adm else 'inadmissible'}")
    adm_all = [x for x in runs
               if x[2] >= Mmax.get(x[3], 10**9)]
    print(f"\nadmissible runs: {len(adm_all)}; max admissible length: "
          f"{max((x[0] for x in adm_all), default=0)}")
    adm_all.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
    print("top 15 admissible runs:")
    for ln, p, q0, cstar in adm_all[:15]:
        print(f"  len={ln:4d} p*={p:6d} q0={q0:6d} cstar={cstar:5d} "
              f"need q0>={Mmax.get(cstar)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    R = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1500
    Q = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 4000
    main(R, Q)

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pure combinatorial test of the C0040 plane-antichain conjecture.

Positions: profiles [c,a,b] (columns of height 3, 2, 1), Young diagrams.
Move (i,j), i in {1,2,3}: columns >= j lose i from their height (floor 0);
prefix columns < j unchanged.  Reachability = transitive closure (game poset).

Question: inside the plane c+a+b = p*, how long can an ANTICHAIN (pairwise
unreachable) be with consecutive q = c+a values (at most one point per q)?
If the max length is a small constant K for all p*, C0039 is pure combinatorics.

Method: for each p*, build all plane points, compute the reachability order
(X <= Y iff Y ->* X), then DP/greedy search for the longest antichain with
consecutive q support.  Reachability: BFS from each point over moves.
"""
import sys
from collections import deque


def moves(pt):
    c, a, b = pt
    out = []
    # prefix determined by cut j-1 = L columns: cp=min(c,L), ap=min(a,max(L-c,0)),
    # bp=min(b, max(L-c-a,0))
    for L in range(0, c + a + b):
        cp = min(c, L)
        ap = min(a, max(L - c, 0))
        bp = min(b, max(L - c - a, 0))
        c2, a2, b2 = c - cp, a - ap, b - bp   # suffix counts by height
        out.append((cp, ap, bp))                  # i=3
        out.append((cp, ap, bp + c2))             # i=2
        out.append((cp, ap + c2, bp + a2))        # i=1
    return out


def reachable_map(pts):
    """desc[Y] = set of X (strictly) reachable from Y; pts list of tuples."""
    idx = {p: k for k, p in enumerate(pts)}
    desc = {}
    for Y in pts:
        seen = set()
        dq = deque(moves(Y))
        while dq:
            X = dq.popleft()
            if X in seen or X == Y:
                continue
            seen.add(X)
            dq.extend(moves(X))
        desc[Y] = {X for X in seen if X in idx}
    return desc


def max_consec_antichain(pts, desc):
    """longest antichain with consecutive q support, at most one per q."""
    byq = {}
    for p in pts:
        byq.setdefault(p[0] + p[1], []).append(p)
    qs = sorted(byq)
    # DP over consecutive q-windows: state = chosen point at current q
    best = (0, None)
    for i in range(len(qs)):
        # extend window from i while q consecutive
        opts = []        # list of per-q candidate lists
        j = i
        while j < len(qs) and (j == i or qs[j] == qs[j-1] + 1):
            opts.append(byq[qs[j]])
            j += 1
        # search longest antichain picking <=1 per column of opts
        # branch and bound: greedy DFS
        def dfs(k, chosen):
            nonlocal best
            if k == len(opts):
                if len(chosen) > best[0]:
                    best = (len(chosen), list(chosen))
                return
            # prune: even taking all remaining can't beat best
            if len(chosen) + (len(opts) - k) <= best[0]:
                return
            for X in opts[k]:
                ok = all(X not in desc[Y] and Y not in desc[X] for Y in chosen)
                if ok:
                    chosen.append(X)
                    dfs(k + 1, chosen)
                    chosen.pop()
            dfs(k + 1, chosen)   # skip this q
        dfs(0, [])
    return best


def main(PMAX):
    for pstar in list(range(1, PMAX + 1)):
        pts = [(c, a, pstar - c - a)
               for c in range(0, pstar + 1) for a in range(0, pstar - c + 1)]
        desc = reachable_map(pts)
        n, arg = max_consec_antichain(pts, desc)
        print(f"p*={pstar:4d}  points={len(pts):5d}  max consec antichain={n}"
              f"  witness={arg}")
        sys.stdout.flush()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 60)

# C0041 -- single-row run lemma (proved)

**Claim.** Fix a row `c` and a value `p*`. Let `S(c, p*) = { q : f(q,c) = p* }`
(valid occurrences, so `p* >= q`). If `q` and `q + t - 1` both lie in
`S(c, p*)` with every intermediate column too (a run of length `t`), and
`q >= N(c)` (the witness row is in its periodic regime at the run's start),
then `t <= p_c`, the period of row `c` (with `p_c := 1` for stale rows, whose
`S` is empty in this regime anyway).

**Proof.** Write `B_c(a) = f(c+a, c) - (c+a)` and `a0 = q - c`. The run says
`B_c(a0 + j) = p* - q - j =: h - j` for `j = 0, ..., t-1` (a unit descent).
`a0 = q - c >= N(c) - c = u_c`, so `B_c` is `p_c`-periodic at `a0`:
`B_c(a0) = B_c(a0 + p_c)`. But the descent chain gives
`B_c(a0 + p_c) = h - p_c` whenever `p_c <= t - 1`, and `h - p_c != h`.
Hence `t - 1 < p_c`, i.e. `t <= p_c`. For a stale row `B_c` is undefined for
`a >= u_c`, so `S(c, p*)` is empty in the regime `q >= N(c)` and the statement
holds vacuously. QED.

**Consequence for C0039.** In a POST-ONSET plug run for row `r` (columns
`q >= max_{c<r} N(c)`), every witness `c < r` satisfies `q >= N(c)`, so each
individual witness row covers at most `p_c <= 9` consecutive columns of the
run (periods to r=50000 are <= 9). The runs of length 459 (C0040) survive only
because their columns sit PRE-onset for their witness rows (e.g. run p*=1106
starts at q=648 while its witness row 647 has N(647) ~ 915 -- the run feeds on
TRANSIENT values of the witness rows). Therefore the whole of C0039 reduces to

<= p_c-consecutive pieces, scattered by the within-period wiggle of
`g_c(q) = q + B_c(q-c)`) jointly cover more than c0 consecutive columns
post-onset? Observed: no (c0 = 6). This is now a statement purely about the
periodic tails `B_c`, which are finite computable objects.

Landing complete at 91% wall clock. Final summary of this last stretch:

**Tested the next concrete thing — the plane-antichain route (C0040) — and refuted it decisively (C0042).** Brute-force BFS on the pure move poset shows max antichains with consecutive `q` inside a plane `c+a+b = p*` are as large as `p*` itself (the `c=0` line is pairwise unreachable), and the P-position plane sections reach 459. No move-structure-only argument can prove the run bound; the mex content is essential.

**But the dissection produced a proved lemma (C0041):** post-onset, each witness row can cover at most `p_c` consecutive columns of a plug run — a unit descent `B_c(a₀+j) = h−j` contradicts `B_c`'s periodicity past `p_c` steps; stale rows cover zero post-onset columns. The 459-long runs survive only *pre*-onset for their witness rows, feeding on transients (run `p*=1106` starts at `q=648` vs `N(647)≈915`).

**The problem is now reduced to its exact finite residue (C0042):** can the level sets of different rows — each a union of ≤ `p_c`-consecutive pieces with positions determined by the periodic tails `B_c` — interleave to cover more than `c0` consecutive columns post-onset? Observed `c0 = 6`; C0041 caps any single row at 9. The direct falsifier to hunt first on a larger table: a post-onset run of length ≥ 10.

Session record: 11 claims (C0032–C0042 + C0028 referee evidence), 8 dead ends, NOTES and HANDOFF current, C0028's proof patched against the referee's one named gap with its rerun queued first next session. The sharpening `N(r) ≤ C·r` now hangs on one crisp, falsifiable interleave question about periodic tails — with its refutation test cheaper than its proof.

The handoff names the exact falsifier hunt: **a post-onset run of length ≥ 10 on a larger table** would be multi-row interleave (C0041 caps single-row coverage at 9) and would stress C0039 to its limit. Testing it now:

   attractors; C0040 run-death: long runs die of validity q>p*, medium runs of

  saturation was mostly the filter. Proof must be uniform in slack.

  `p_r | s` proved in Addendum 2.

   `python -u -m harness.referee C0028 --root . --max-spend 0.45`

   first — C0028 has one, C0024 does not and its dependency statements leak
   narrative). The referee needs ~40-60 min for its 80 turns; do not bound it
   below that. t=0.3 may fail to finish (network flakiness observed) — rerun

   census past r=50000 and re-run `scratch/hunt_full.cpp`; record the max
   before stating any sharp K. An octad falsifies the absolute-constant
   conjecture and with it the `N(r) <= K r` route via plug runs.

   matches (rows c, values `g_c(q)=q+B_c(q-c)`, one column per row) can cover
   8 consecutive columns — uniformly in slack (per C0044's correction), with
   the 75821 heptads as the sharp cases. Attack via SAT/ILP over
   (period, phase, values) tuples or the mex structure of the tails directly.
   At c0=7 this yields `N(r) <= 9r` (empirically `N(r) <= 2r`).

zero counterexamples), falsifier precisely defined and cheap, sharp cases
enumerated. What would kill it: an 8-run in extended tails; note the constant
has drifted 5->6->7 with range, so do not hard-code 7 in any theorem statement
beyond "absolute constant (currently 7 on all available data)". C0028's bound
survived adversarial self-review and one referee pass (accept_with_gaps, gap
patched); its only remaining risk is referee scrutiny of C0024's (ii)-(iii),

this session. Session discipline note: three self-interpretations were
overturned by population checks (C0043, C0044, c0 constants) — the next
session should keep testing extremal-example stories on populations before
building on them.

   attractors; C0040 run-death: long runs die of validity q>p*, medium runs of
